subject: Clarify p50/p95 measurement approach for Hosted API SLA
messages:
From: Elena Martin <elena@opaltech.io>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@opaltech.io
Date: 2026-09-25T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Clarify p50/p95 measurement for Hosted API SLA

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo — OpalTech is excited about the performance profile you showed. Before we proceed to legal, our compliance team needs a clear definition of how Redwood measures p50 and p95 for the hosted API. Specifically:

- What is the measurement window (rolling 1h, fixed 24h, other)?
- How are short-lived spikes and maintenance windows treated (carveouts)?
- For streaming responses, which token(s) count toward latency?
- Sampling cadence and whether you publish per-region percentiles or global.

We have a clause in our procurement that requires a 30-day sample of evidence and a mutual action plan for any temporary exceptions. Can you send a short playbook we can include in the SOW that lays this out? Also please include any limitations (e.g., batched jobs, asynchronous callbacks).

Appreciate a reply this week if possible — we are trying to keep the procurement timeline tight.

Best,
Elena
Elena Martin
Director, Cloud Ops | OpalTech

Subject: Re: Request: Clarify p50/p95 measurement for Hosted API SLA

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick acknowledgement: happy to provide a playbook and a 30-day evidence bundle. I've looped in Marissa (AE) and Karthik (infra) to help define the measurement rules and what we can commit to in the SOW.

High-level proposal we can start from (we'll refine):
- Measurement: rolling 1-hour window computed from 5-minute buckets sampled every minute (see attached draft playbook).
- Percentiles: p50/p95 will be computed per-region and published daily; global view available for operational dashboards.
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance windows, region-level outages, and provider maintenance will be excluded subject to advance notice/process.
- Streaming: for streaming endpoints we will use first-token time as primary latency metric; full-stream completion times can be reported separately.

Attaching an initial playbook draft (redwood_slo_playbook_draft.pdf) and a short measurement spec spreadsheet. Karthik — can you confirm the streaming-first-token rule and the threshold for excluding long-running/queued jobs?

Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-27T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Clarify p50/p95 measurement for Hosted API SLA

Elena —

I wanted to propose concrete numbers so procurement can move forward while engineering validates edge cases:

Proposal (commercial):
- p50 target: 60 ms (per-region)
- p95 target: 250 ms (per-region)
- Measurement window: rolling 1-hour, composed of twelve 5-minute sampling buckets (we sample every minute within those buckets).
- Evidence: daily exported percentile reports + 30-day historical CSV on request.
- Temporary exceptions: up to 4 hours of scheduled maintenance per region per month, and emergency carveouts for cloud provider incidents (formal RCA to follow).

Operational notes:
- We recommend per-route SLOs for routes that do heavy batching (e.g., bulk embeddings) and a global SLO for realtime text-generation routes.
- If you need a stricter window (e.g., fixed daily measurement), we can include that as a contract addendum with a short pilot.

I've attached a short spreadsheet that maps request types to suggested measurement treatment (measurement_specs.xlsx). If the numbers above look ok I can draft the SOW language and DocuSign amendment.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Quick technical clarifications for the playbook and SOW language — Elena, copying them here so procurement has the exact rules we'll use when we assemble the evidence CSVs: 

1) Sampling and buckets
- We sample all incoming requests and record request_start and first_token_emit timestamps. Buckets are 5-minute sliding; within each 5-minute bucket we compute percentiles from raw samples and then roll those into the 1-hour rolling window by taking the union of the twelve buckets.

2) Streaming endpoints
- We measure first-token latency for p50/p95. If a customer requests full-stream latency reporting, we will provide that as an additional metric but it will not be used for the p50/p95 SLA.

3) Batched & async jobs
- Server-side batching (auto-batching inside Redwood runtime) will be measured against a per-route SLO where applicable. Asynchronous callbacks and background ingestion jobs (non-API requests) are excluded from the hosted-API SLO.

4) Exclusions and thresholds
- We will exclude requests flagged as "synthetic" or from our canary pool.
- Any single request with observed latency > 15s is excluded from percentile computation (these are considered outliers and handled in separate error/timeout SLOs).

5) Carveout process
- Emergency carveouts will be declared by Redwood ops (posting an incident notice and an initial carveout window in the customer console); RCAs will be produced within 7 business days. Scheduled maintenance will be posted 72 hours in advance where possible.

If these rules align with OpalTech's needs I'll update the playbook and produce the 30-day raw CSV export once we have signature.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
